MED001.mechanism_of_action: Centrally inhibits prostaglandin synthesis through COX-3 / peroxidase modulation, blocking spinal pain impulse generation and resetting the hypothalamic thermoregulatory center.
MED001.uses: Relief of mild to moderate pain (headache, musculoskeletal pain, dysmenorrhea, dental ache) and reduction of fever.
MED001.off_label_uses: Post-immunization febrile prophylaxis in pediatric populations under clinical guidance.
MED001.side_effects: Generally well-tolerated at therapeutic dosages. Occasional nausea, dyspepsia, or allergic dermatological reactions.
MED001.less_common_side_effects: Transient thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, mild epigastric discomfort.
MED001.serious_adverse_effects: Acute hepatotoxicity (hepatic necrosis) upon overdose (>4000 mg/24h or in chronic alcoholism), acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, anaphylactic shock.
MED001.contraindications: Severe active hepatic impairment, decompensated liver disease, known hypersensitivity to paracetamol.
MED001.allergies_warning: Discontinue immediately if skin reddening, rash, or facial edema develops.

interactions.risk: Potentiates CYP2E1-mediated hepatotoxic NAPQI accumulation, increasing risk of fatal hepatic failure.
Prolonged regular high-dose intake increases international normalized ratio (INR) and bleeding risks.
Increases hepatotoxicity risk through enzymatic induction.

MED001.precautions: Do not exceed 4000 mg in 24 hours. Check all concurrent cough/cold medications to prevent unintentional toxic acetaminophen doubling.
MED001.pregnancy_warning: Considered the safest analgesic in pregnancy when clinically indicated, used at the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration.
MED001.breastfeeding_warning: Excreted in breast milk in clinically insignificant quantities; compatible with breastfeeding.
MED001.pediatric_warning: Administer weight-based dosing (10-15 mg/kg/dose) every 4-6 hours. Avoid adult formulations in infants.
MED001.storage: Store below 30°C in a dry place protected from direct sunlight and moisture.

MED002.mechanism_of_action: Binds reversibly to the 50S ribosomal subunit of susceptible microorganisms, inhibiting translocation and terminating bacterial protein synthesis.
MED002.uses: Treatment of susceptible bacterial respiratory infections, pertussis, chlamydial infections, diphtheria, and skin/soft tissue infections.
MED002.off_label_uses: Gastrointestinal prokinetic agent in gastroparesis due to motilin receptor agonism.
MED002.side_effects: Gastrointestinal distress, epigastric cramps, nausea, vomiting, flatulence, diarrhea.
MED002.less_common_side_effects: Transient hearing impairment with high intravenous doses, cholestatic hepatitis.
MED002.serious_adverse_effects: QT interval prolongation, Torsades de Pointes ventricular arrhythmia, Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea (pseudomembranous colitis), severe hepatotoxicity.
MED002.contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to erythromycin or macrolides; concurrent therapy with cisapride, pimozide, astemizole, terfenadine, or ergotamine.
MED002.allergies_warning: Cross-reactivity occurs across all macrolide class antibiotics (azithromycin, clarithromycin).

interactions.risk: Inhibits CYP3A4, causing massive statin accumulation, rhabdomyolysis, and acute renal failure.
Decreases theophylline clearance leading to potentially toxic bronchodilator serum concentrations.
Inhibits warfarin metabolism, significantly increasing prothrombin time and hemorrhage risk.

MED002.precautions: CRITICAL ANTIBIOTIC ALERT: Must complete the full clinical duration as prescribed. Incomplete courses cause antibiotic resistance. Take on an empty stomach or 1 hour before meals.
MED002.pregnancy_warning: Estolate salt formulation is contraindicated in pregnancy due to increased incidence of reversible cholestatic hepatitis.
MED002.breastfeeding_warning: Compatible with maternal breastfeeding; monitor infant for gastrointestinal disturbances.
MED002.pediatric_warning: Associated with infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis when administered to neonates under 2 weeks.
MED002.storage: Store below 25°C in original moisture-tight packaging.

MED003.mechanism_of_action: Irreversibly acetylates serine-529 of cyclooxygenase-1 (COX-1), blocking platelet thromboxane A2 synthesis for the platelet lifespan (7-10 days), thereby preventing platelet aggregation.
MED003.uses: Temporary relief of headache, toothache, musculoskeletal ache, arthritis; secondary cardiovascular prophylaxis in coronary artery disease.
MED003.off_label_uses: Colorectal cancer prophylaxis in selected high-risk cohorts; preeclampsia prevention in high-risk pregnancies under obstetric oversight.
MED003.side_effects: Dyspepsia, heartburn, epigastric discomfort, minor bleeding, bruising.
MED003.less_common_side_effects: Tinnitus (at elevated doses), occult GI blood loss, bronchospasm in triad asthma.
MED003.serious_adverse_effects: Major gastrointestinal ulceration and hemorrhage, hemorrhagic stroke, Reye's syndrome in children/adolescents with viral illness.
MED003.contraindications: Active peptic ulcer disease, bleeding diathesis, hemophilia, aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease (Samter's triad), children under 16 years with viral fevers.
MED003.allergies_warning: Cross-sensitivity with other NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen). Seek immediate care if wheezing or angioedema occurs.

interactions.risk: Synergistic inhibition of hemostasis resulting in severe life-threatening internal bleeding.
Competitively blocks aspirin's access to platelet COX-1, attenuating aspirin's cardioprotective antiplatelet effect.
Decreases renal excretion of methotrexate, causing severe hematologic toxicity.

MED003.precautions: BLEEDING RISK ALERT: Stop therapy at least 7 days before elective surgeries. Discontinue immediately if black tarry stools or hematemesis appears.
MED003.pregnancy_warning: Contraindicated in the third trimester of pregnancy (causes premature closure of ductus arteriosus and prolonged labor).
MED003.breastfeeding_warning: Avoid during lactation; salicylates excrete into breast milk and pose metabolic risks.
MED003.pediatric_warning: DO NOT ADMINISTER TO CHILDREN OR TEENAGERS WITH CHICKENPOX OR FLU SYMPTOMS (risk of fatal Reye's syndrome).
MED003.storage: Store tightly sealed in a dry place at 15-30°C. Protect from dampness which hydrolyzes aspirin to acetic acid.

MED004.mechanism_of_action: Scavenges reactive oxygen species (free radicals) in cellular lipid bilayers, terminating lipid peroxidation chain reactions and maintaining structural membrane integrity.
MED004.uses: Treatment and prevention of Vitamin E deficiency, abetalipoproteinemia, cystic fibrosis-associated malabsorption, and peripheral neuropathy.
MED004.off_label_uses: Adjuvant dermatological and nocturnal leg cramp therapy under nutritional supervision.
MED004.side_effects: Rarely causes adverse effects at standard nutritional dosages. Mild nausea, diarrhea, fatigue, or headache reported with supra-therapeutic intake.
MED004.less_common_side_effects: Transient visual disturbances, abdominal cramps, gonadal dysfunction at megadoses.
MED004.serious_adverse_effects: High-dose chronic consumption (>800 IU/day) increases all-cause mortality, hemorrhagic stroke risks, and impairs blood coagulation.
MED004.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to tocopheryl acetate or gelatin capsule excipients, active bleeding disorders.
MED004.allergies_warning: Softgel gelatin shell contains animal-derived bovine/porcine components.

interactions.risk: Antagonizes vitamin K-dependent clotting factors, potentiating bleeding risks at doses >400 IU.
Impairs intestinal absorption of fat-soluble vitamin E.
High-dose antioxidants may theoretically attenuate therapeutic oxidative tumor cell killing.

MED004.precautions: Take with fatty meals for optimal lipid absorption. Do not consume excessive megadoses beyond prescribed physician directives.
MED004.pregnancy_warning: Safe at recommended dietary allowance (RDA 15 mg/day). High-dose supplementation in pregnancy must be physician-monitored.
MED004.breastfeeding_warning: Excreted in breast milk; compatible with lactation at physiological requirements.
MED004.pediatric_warning: Use pediatric formulations; avoid high-dose softgels in neonates due to risk of necrotizing enterocolitis.
MED004.storage: Store below 25°C in a dry place. Protect softgels from direct heat and freezing.

MED005.mechanism_of_action: Central inhibition of prostaglandin synthesis in brain and spinal cord, exerting potent antipyretic action through hypothalamic heat regulation.
MED005.uses: Moderate fever associated with viral illness, post-vaccine fever, body aches, severe tension headache, toothache.
MED005.off_label_uses: Mild osteoarthritis joint pain flare management.
MED005.side_effects: Mild epigastric sensation, nausea. Very safe at standard dosage.
MED005.serious_adverse_effects: Hepatotoxicity upon acute toxic accumulation (>4000 mg/day).
MED005.contraindications: Active severe hepatic failure, alcoholism, paracetamol hypersensitivity.
MED005.allergies_warning: Seek emergency care if cutaneous erythema or breathing restriction develops.

interactions.risk: Excessive CYP2E1 NAPQI generation; increased liver necrosis risk.
Mild anticoagulant potentiating effect with continuous daily use.

MED005.precautions: Maximum 3 to 4 tablets (1950 - 2600 mg) per day for adults. Maintain a minimum 6-hour interval between doses.
MED005.pregnancy_warning: Safe in pregnancy at lowest therapeutic dose when indicated.
MED005.pediatric_warning: 650 mg tablet is intended for adults and adolescents >12 years (>40 kg). Do not administer whole tablet to young children.
MED005.storage: Store in a cool dry place below 30°C.

MED006.mechanism_of_action: Amoxicillin inhibits bacterial cell wall biosynthesis by binding to penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs). Clavulanic acid irreversibly inhibits bacterial beta-lactamase enzymes, protecting amoxicillin from enzymatic degradation.
MED006.uses: Treatment of acute bacterial sinusitis, community-acquired pneumonia, otitis media, recurrent tonsillitis, complicated urinary tract infections, and skin/soft tissue infections.
MED006.off_label_uses: Animal bite wound prophylaxis and dental abscess eradication.
MED006.side_effects: Diarrhea (frequent due to clavulanic acid), nausea, vomiting, candidiasis (oral/vaginal thrush).
MED006.less_common_side_effects: Headache, mild dizziness, superficial tooth discoloration.
MED006.serious_adverse_effects: Anaphylaxis and angioedema, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, cholestatic jaundice / acute hepatic dysfunction, Clostridioides difficile colitis.
MED006.contraindications: History of amoxicillin-clavulanate-associated jaundice or severe hepatic dysfunction; history of severe immediate beta-lactam hypersensitivity (anaphylaxis).
MED006.allergies_warning: PENICILLIN ALLERGY ALERT: Immediate life-threatening anaphylaxis may occur in penicillin-allergic patients.

interactions.risk: Decreases renal tubular excretion of methotrexate, increasing toxic myelosuppression.
High incidence of generalized erythematous maculopapular rash.
Alters gut flora synthesizing vitamin K, prolonging prothrombin time.

MED006.precautions: CRITICAL FIXED-DOSE COMBINATION ANTIBIOTIC: Complete entire 5-7 day prescribed cycle. Take at the start of a meal to minimize gastrointestinal upset and maximize clavulanate bioavailability.
MED006.pregnancy_warning: Generally safe in pregnancy; prophylactic use in preterm rupture of membranes may be avoided due to neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis risk.
MED006.breastfeeding_warning: Both agents enter breast milk in trace amounts; monitor infant for loose stools and oral candida.
MED006.pediatric_warning: Use oral suspensions formulated specifically for weight-based pediatric dosing.
MED006.storage: Store in moisture-proof foil below 25°C. Desiccant in bottle/strip must be kept dry.

MED007.mechanism_of_action: Dual complementary pain-pathway modulation: Ibuprofen acts peripherally by inhibiting COX-1 and COX-2 enzymes to reduce inflammatory prostanoids; Paracetamol acts centrally on descending serotonergic and endocannabinoid pathways.
MED007.uses: Moderate musculoskeletal pain, dental extraction pain, dysmenorrhea, post-traumatic soft-tissue inflammation, arthralgia.
MED007.side_effects: Gastric irritation, epigastric heartburn, nausea, indigestion, dizziness.
MED007.less_common_side_effects: Tinnitus, mild peripheral edema, constipation or diarrhea.
MED007.serious_adverse_effects: Peptic ulcer perforation, acute gastrointestinal hemorrhage, acute renal failure, cardiovascular thrombotic events.
MED007.contraindications: Active gastric ulcer or history of GI bleeding, severe renal or hepatic failure, third trimester of pregnancy, aspirin-sensitive asthma.
MED007.allergies_warning: Do not consume if allergic to either ibuprofen, paracetamol, or aspirin.

interactions.risk: Exponential increase in gastrointestinal ulceration and mucosal bleeding.
Attenuates antihypertensive effectiveness and precipitates acute kidney injury (triple whammy with diuretics).
Reduces renal lithium clearance, inducing severe lithium neurotoxicity.

MED007.precautions: Take strictly after meals with water. Do not combine with other paracetamol products. Avoid alcohol consumption.
MED007.pregnancy_warning: CONTRAINDICATED in third trimester of pregnancy due to risk of premature ductus arteriosus closure.
MED007.breastfeeding_warning: Both agents present in minimal amounts in breast milk; short-term use acceptable under medical advice.
MED007.pediatric_warning: Not recommended for children under 12 years of age.
MED007.storage: Store in a cool dry place away from direct heat and light.

MED008.mechanism_of_action: Pantoprazole suppresses gastric acid secretion by specific inhibition of the H+/K+-ATPase enzyme system at the secretory surface of the parietal cell. Domperidone facilitates gastric emptying and increases lower esophageal sphincter tone by blocking peripheral dopamine D2 receptors.
MED008.uses: Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), acid-induced dyspepsia, reflux esophagitis, non-ulcer dyspepsia with delayed gastric emptying.
MED008.side_effects: Dry mouth, headache, transient diarrhea, abdominal discomfort, flatulence.
MED008.serious_adverse_effects: Cardiac QT prolongation and serious ventricular arrhythmias (domperidone high dose), hypomagnesemia, Clostridioides difficile diarrhea, osteoporotic fractures with prolonged PPI therapy.
MED008.contraindications: Prolonged cardiac QT interval or underlying cardiac arrhythmias, prolactin-releasing pituitary tumor, mechanical gastrointestinal obstruction or perforation.
MED008.allergies_warning: Hypersensitivity to pantoprazole, substituted benzimidazoles, or domperidone.

interactions.risk: Inhibits domperidone metabolism and reduces antifungal absorption due to elevated gastric pH.
Minimal interaction compared to omeprazole, but monitor antiplatelet effectiveness.
Additive QT prolongation and risk of Torsades de Pointes.

MED008.precautions: Take once daily in the morning, exactly 30 to 60 minutes BEFORE breakfast. Do not crush or chew capsule pellets.
MED008.pregnancy_warning: Use only if the potential benefit justifies potential fetal risk under physician prescription.
MED008.breastfeeding_warning: Domperidone is excreted in small amounts in breast milk; evaluate risk-benefit.
MED008.pediatric_warning: Safety and effectiveness not established in pediatric patients.
MED008.storage: Store below 25°C in original moisture-tight aluminum foil.

MED009.mechanism_of_action: Selectively blocks the binding of angiotensin II to the AT1 receptor in vascular smooth muscle and adrenal gland, inhibiting vasoconstriction and aldosterone-secreting effects. Also acts as a partial agonist of PPAR-gamma.
MED009.uses: Essential hypertension management, cardiovascular risk reduction in patients unable to take ACE inhibitors, diabetic nephropathy.
MED009.side_effects: Dizziness, lightheadedness, fatigue, back pain, sinus congestion.
MED009.less_common_side_effects: Hypotension on first dose, orthostasis, diarrhea.
MED009.serious_adverse_effects: Hyperkalemia (elevated potassium), acute kidney failure (in bilateral renal artery stenosis), angioedema.
MED009.contraindications: Pregnancy (Black Box Warning: fetal toxicity and death), bilateral renal artery stenosis, severe hepatic impairment or biliary obstruction.
MED009.allergies_warning: Discontinue immediately if swelling of lips, tongue, or pharynx occurs.

interactions.risk: Severe hyperkalemia leading to cardiac arrest.
Blunts antihypertensive action and precipitates acute renal failure.
Increases serum lithium concentrations and toxicity.

MED009.precautions: BLACK BOX WARNING: Discontinue immediately if pregnancy is detected. Monitor serum creatinine and potassium regularly.
MED009.pregnancy_warning: CONTRAINDICATED IN PREGNANCY (causes fetal renal failure, oligohydramnios, skull hypoplasia, and fetal death).
MED009.breastfeeding_warning: Not recommended during breastfeeding; alternative antihypertensives preferred.
MED009.pediatric_warning: Safety and efficacy not established in pediatric cohorts.

MED010.mechanism_of_action: Metformin reduces hepatic gluconeogenesis and intestinal glucose absorption while improving peripheral insulin sensitivity. Glimepiride stimulates insulin release from pancreatic beta cells by binding to sulfonylurea receptors and closing ATP-sensitive potassium channels.
MED010.uses: Second-line treatment of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus when diet, exercise, and single-agent metformin are insufficient for glycemic control.
MED010.side_effects: Hypoglycemia (sweating, tremor, hunger), gastrointestinal distress, metallic taste, nausea, flatulence.
MED010.less_common_side_effects: Vitamin B12 deficiency (with long-term metformin), weight gain.
MED010.serious_adverse_effects: Severe hypoglycemia (coma/seizures), Metformin-induced Lactic Acidosis (rare but fatal), hemolytic anemia in G6PD deficiency.
MED010.contraindications: Type 1 Diabetes, severe renal failure (eGFR <30 mL/min), acute metabolic acidosis, severe infection, intravascular iodinated contrast administration.

interactions.risk: Precipitates acute renal dysfunction and lactic acidosis; hold medicine 48 hours prior to scan.
Masks adrenergic warning symptoms of hypoglycemia (tachycardia, tremor).
Potentiates severe hypoglycemia and increases lactic acidosis risk.

MED010.precautions: Take strictly with or immediately before the first main meal of the day. Keep fast-acting carbohydrates (sugar candies/glucose) available for hypoglycemic emergencies.
MED010.pregnancy_warning: Insulin is the preferred antidiabetic agent during pregnancy; discontinue combination therapy.
MED010.breastfeeding_warning: Not recommended; potential risk of neonatal hypoglycemia.
MED010.pediatric_warning: Not indicated for pediatric type 2 diabetes.
MED010.storage: Store in a dry place below 25°C.

MED011.mechanism_of_action: Inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase (topoisomerase II) and topoisomerase IV, preventing bacterial DNA replication, transcription, repair, and recombination.
MED011.uses: Complicated urinary tract infections, infectious diarrhea, typhoid fever, intra-abdominal infections, bone and joint infections.
MED011.side_effects: Nausea, diarrhea, abdominal pain, headache, sleep disturbances.
MED011.serious_adverse_effects: BLACK BOX WARNINGS: Tendon rupture / tendonitis (Achilles tendon), peripheral neuropathy, central nervous system toxicities (seizures, hallucinations), aortic aneurysm rupture.
MED011.contraindications: History of quinolone-associated tendon rupture, concurrent administration with tizanidine, myasthenia gravis.
MED011.allergies_warning: Cross-sensitivity across all quinolones (levofloxacin, moxifloxacin, ofloxacin).

interactions.risk: Forms insoluble chelate complexes, abolishing ciprofloxacin gastrointestinal absorption.
Inhibits CYP1A2, elevating theophylline serum levels to neurotoxic concentrations.
Significantly amplifies anticoagulant effect; monitor INR.

MED011.precautions: CRITICAL ANTIBIOTIC: Maintain adequate hydration to prevent crystalluria. Separate intake from antacids, milk, or calcium-fortified juices by at least 2 hours.
MED011.pregnancy_warning: Generally avoided in pregnancy due to cartilage damage observed in juvenile animal studies.
MED011.breastfeeding_warning: Excreted in breast milk; consider alternative antibiotic or interrupt nursing.
MED011.pediatric_warning: Avoid in children <18 years except for specific indications (complicated UTI, anthrax) due to arthropathy.
MED011.storage: Store below 25°C in original dry packaging.

MED012.mechanism_of_action: Binds reversibly to the 50S ribosomal subunit of susceptible microorganisms, inhibiting transpeptidation and protein translation.
MED012.uses: Upper and lower respiratory tract infections, acute bacterial sinusitis, tonsillitis, community-acquired pneumonia, skin infections, chlamydia trachomatis urethritis.
MED012.off_label_uses: Babesiosis, traveler's diarrhea prophylaxis in refractory regions.
MED012.side_effects: Diarrhea, loose stools, nausea, vomiting, abdominal cramps.
MED012.serious_adverse_effects: Cardiac QT prolongation, Torsades de Pointes, Clostridioides difficile colitis, cholestatic jaundice / liver necrosis.
MED012.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to azithromycin, erythromycin, or any macrolide; history of cholestatic jaundice associated with prior azithromycin therapy.

interactions.risk: Reduces peak serum concentration of azithromycin; separate dosing by 2 hours.
Elevates digoxin serum levels by altering intestinal flora and P-glycoprotein transport.
Elevated risk of fatal cardiac dysrhythmias.

MED012.precautions: CRITICAL ANTIBIOTIC: Take 1 hour before or 2 hours after food for optimal absorption. Complete the entire 3-day or 5-day regimen.
MED012.pregnancy_warning: Category B. Animal studies reveal no evidence of harm; use when clearly prescribed by an obstetrician.
MED012.breastfeeding_warning: Excreted in low amounts in breast milk; monitor infant for gastrointestinal effects.
MED012.pediatric_warning: Syrups and pediatric suspensions available for weight-adjusted dosing.
MED012.storage: Store in a cool dry place below 25°C.

MED013.mechanism_of_action: Dextromethorphan suppresses the medullary cough center via sigma-1 and NMDA receptor modulation. Phenylephrine causes vasoconstriction in nasal mucosa, reducing congestion. Chlorpheniramine competitively antagonizes histamine H1 receptors, alleviating sneezing and rhinorrhea.
MED013.uses: Symptomatic relief of dry, unproductive cough associated with allergic rhinitis, viral upper respiratory infections, and environmental irritants.
MED013.side_effects: Drowsiness, dry mouth, blurred vision, mild nausea, constipation.
MED013.less_common_side_effects: Elevated blood pressure, urinary retention, restlessness or insomnia.
MED013.serious_adverse_effects: Serotonin syndrome (when combined with MAO inhibitors), severe hypertension crisis, central nervous system depression.
MED013.contraindications: Severe hypertension, severe coronary artery disease, closed-angle glaucoma, concurrent or recent (within 14 days) use of Monoamine Oxidase Inhibitors (MAOIs).
MED013.allergies_warning: Discontinue if urticaria, facial swelling, or breathing difficulty occurs.

interactions.risk: Life-threatening Serotonin Syndrome and severe hypertensive crisis.
Severe additive central nervous system depression and psychomotor impairment.
Increases dextromethorphan levels and serotonin toxicity.

MED013.precautions: LIQUID SYRUP FORMULATION: Shake well before measuring. Do NOT operate motor vehicles or heavy machinery due to prominent sedation risk. Not for productive (wet) phlegm cough.
MED013.pregnancy_warning: Consult doctor; avoid in first trimester unless clinically essential.
MED013.breastfeeding_warning: Antihistamines and phenylephrine may reduce milk supply and cause infant sedation.
MED013.pediatric_warning: Contraindicated in children under 4 years of age; risk of life-threatening respiratory depression.
MED013.storage: Store below 25°C in original carton protected from light.

MED014.mechanism_of_action: Binds covalently to the gastric H+/K+-ATPase proton pump on gastric parietal cells, blocking the final step of acid secretion.
MED014.uses: Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), erosive esophagitis, gastric and duodenal ulcers, Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, NSAID-induced ulcer prophylaxis.
MED014.off_label_uses: Stress ulcer prophylaxis in critically ill patients.
MED014.side_effects: Headache, diarrhea, constipation, abdominal pain, flatulence.
MED014.serious_adverse_effects: Clostridioides difficile diarrhea, hypomagnesemia, acute interstitial nephritis, increased fracture risk with long-term use.
MED014.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to pantoprazole or other substituted benzimidazoles.

interactions.risk: Significantly impairs antifungal absorption due to neutral gastric pH.
Elevates and prolongs methotrexate serum levels, increasing toxicity.

MED014.precautions: Swallow tablet whole with water 30-60 minutes before breakfast. Do not crush, break, or chew the enteric coating.
MED014.pregnancy_warning: Category B. Animal studies show no teratogenicity; use when clinically indicated.
MED014.breastfeeding_warning: Excreted in low concentrations in breast milk; evaluate benefit-risk.
MED014.pediatric_warning: Approved for adolescents >=12 years for erosive GERD.
MED014.storage: Store in a cool dry place below 30°C.

MED015.mechanism_of_action: Selectively and competitively inhibits HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme converting HMG-CoA to mevalonate, upregulating hepatic LDL receptors and clearing circulating LDL cholesterol.
MED015.uses: Primary and secondary prevention of cardiovascular events, hypercholesterolemia, mixed dyslipidemia, hypertriglyceridemia.
MED015.side_effects: Myalgia (muscle ache), nasopharyngitis, arthralgia, diarrhea, dyspepsia.
MED015.less_common_side_effects: Elevated hepatic transaminases, insomnia, peripheral neuropathy.
MED015.serious_adverse_effects: Rhabdomyolysis with myoglobinuria and acute renal failure, immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy, severe hepatotoxicity.
MED015.contraindications: Active liver disease, unexplained persistent elevation of serum transaminases, pregnancy, lactation.
MED015.allergies_warning: Discontinue if unexplained diffuse muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness develops, especially with fever.

interactions.risk: Potent CYP3A4 inhibition elevates atorvastatin plasma concentrations, precipitating severe rhabdomyolysis.
Inhibits intestinal CYP3A4, increasing statin exposure.
Massively elevates statin concentration and myopathy risk.

MED015.precautions: Take once daily with or without food, at the same time each day (evening preferred). Report unexplained muscle soreness immediately.
MED015.pregnancy_warning: ABSOLUTELY CONTRAINDICATED IN PREGNANCY (disrupts fetal cholesterol biosynthesis; teratogenic).
MED015.breastfeeding_warning: Contraindicated; statins are excreted in human milk and affect infant lipid metabolism.
MED015.pediatric_warning: Approved for heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia in pediatric patients >=10 years.

MED016.mechanism_of_action: Central inhibition of cyclooxygenase, blocking prostaglandin synthesis in the brain and spinal cord, exerting analgesia and lowering setpoint in the hypothalamus.
MED016.uses: Mild to moderate pain relief (fever, headache, toothache, muscle aches, dysmenorrhea).
MED016.serious_adverse_effects: Hepatotoxicity upon acute toxic accumulation (>4000 mg/day).
MED016.contraindications: Severe liver failure, known paracetamol hypersensitivity.

interactions.risk: Increased liver toxicity risk.
Slight INR elevation with long-term daily use.

MED016.precautions: Do not exceed 4000 mg per day. Check all concurrent OTC medications.
MED016.pregnancy_warning: Safe in pregnancy at lowest effective dose.
MED016.pediatric_warning: Use pediatric syrup or drops for children under 12 years.
MED016.storage: Store below 25°C in a dry place.
